item.title: A day of analogue development: rain, Zenit cameras and a real passion for photography
item.description:
On 2 February we ran the introduction to development workshop at Cameras & Films (the former Lomography Embassy Barcelona). It was raining.

The students headed out into the streets of the Born with Zenit cameras fitted with Helios lenses and Fomapan 100. Because the light was poor, we pushed it to ISO 800. Twenty minutes on the street, then back to the lab.

From there on: loading the spiral, mixing the chemistry, developing. Ninety minutes of the complete process.

item.title: Introduction to analogue photography workshop results
item.description:
Results from the latest introduction workshop. The students worked with a Rolleiflex f/3.5 and Fomapan 100 — and developed the roll during the same session.

There is something very concrete about seeing for the first time how an image appears on negatives you exposed yourself.

item.title: Results from the Large Format workshop
item.description:
Results from the introductory Large Format workshop at Llumàtics.

4×5" black-and-white sheet film, developed in a tray. The image quality that large format delivers is hard to explain until you have it in your hands.

item.title: Large Format workshop — behind the scenes
item.description:
This is how Saturday’s workshop at Llumàtics went.

The large format camera, 4×5" sheets, the ground glass, the black cloth over the head. The full ritual of large format photography, compressed into a single morning.
